clue.text: In retreat, give support to accommodation for the sick

parts.note: to back someone is to give them support
hospital wards house patients who are ill

explanation.surface: Someone backs a plan for housing patients while the cause is losing ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving in retreat is going the other way, rearwards, away from the front.

clue.text: Bob sure to be heading for the border

definitions.meaning: to bob is to move up and down, to leap or spring
certain, as in 'it is ... to happen'

explanation.definitionFit: Bound covers a leap, a certainty and a destination, three distinct senses of one word.

clue.text: Fool wearing bird's robe

indicators.note: wearing says one piece has the other on, so it is put round it

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot dresses in a bird's gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird's' looks possessive, but it just supplies the male bird that does the wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock is a long garment worn by clergy, a clerical robe.

clue.text: Discombobulated—-he was, with an overwhelming defeat

indicators.note: discombobulated means confused, so the words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man was thrown into confusion after a crushing loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash in sport is a rout where the loser fails to score at all.

clue.text: Rating's hair tousled, but perfectly OK

indicators.note: tousled means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's counts here, giving RATINGS

explanation.surface: A sailor's hair is a mess, but he is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in good order, fit and well.

clue.text: Drink is splendid, no hesitation

indicators.note: no says the following piece is taken away

parts.note: super means splendid
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A drink is excellent, and someone says so without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to take liquid in sips, to drink.

clue.text: Rasher company restrained by injunction

indicators.note: restrained by says one piece is held within another, kept in check inside it

parts.note: an injunction is an order forbidding something, a ban

explanation.surface: A firm is stopped by a court order from doing something rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rasher' looks like a comparative of rash, but it is the noun: a slice of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a thin slice of cured pork, so the meat it is cut from serves as the definition by example.

clue.text: Can/Will start to yodel

parts.note: Bill and Will are both pet forms of William

indicators.note: start to says take the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Will may begin to yodel.
explanation.walkthrough: A billy or billycan is a tin cooking pot used by campers in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy is a metal pot used for boiling water over a campfire.

clue.text: Campanologist with a wild dream

parts.note: a campanologist rings bells, a chimer

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer has a fanciful vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an impossible fancy, an illusion or pipe dream.

clue.text: Reputation — one I try to reform

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tries to repair a damaged name.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame of the wrong kind, a bad name or ill repute.

clue.text: Improvement of side after 5 changes

indicators.note: after puts the side piece behind the rearranged letters
changes says the letters of the answer to clue 5 are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 5 down is SUP
a wing is one side of a team, a building or an army

explanation.surface: A team's results improve once its fifth man changes ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SUP, the answer to 5 down, into UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An upswing is an upward trend, a rise or improvement in fortunes.

clue.text: A practitioner of chiromancy making some archetypal mistakes

indicators.note: making some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller who reads hands commits a few classic blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiromancy is hand-reading, so someone who practises it is a reader of palms.

clue.text: Wild dog died beside its earth

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees
an earth is the burrow an animal such as a fox lives in, a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A wild dog dies next to its own den.
explanation.definitionFit: The dhole is an Asian wild canine that hunts in packs.

clue.text: Toy gives rise to debt ready for settlement

indicators.note: for settlement suggests the words are to be settled into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A toy prompts a debt that is ready to be paid off.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a soft stuffed plaything shaped like a bear.

clue.text: Upset, did he thirst to spread malicious gossip?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who wants to spread rumours about others.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish the dirt is an idiom for passing on scandalous gossip.

clue.text: Bird emerging from a country

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom, a country

explanation.surface: A bird emerges from somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The auk is a diving seabird of northern waters, such as the razorbill or puffin.

clue.text: Stars accompanying capital lawyer

parts.note: and means along with, accompanying
Rome is the capital of Italy
DA, district attorney, is a lawyer in the US

explanation.surface: Celebrities go out with a metropolitan attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Dispatch a vessel, a ship inherited, short of a name

parts.note: SS, short for steamship, is a vessel
SS, steamship, again

indicators.note: short of says the word is missing one of its letters

parts.note: an innate quality is one inborn, inherited

explanation.surface: Someone sends off a boat and a ship that they came into, lacking a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of a name' takes one N from INNATE, leaving INATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone can mean to kill them, and assassinate means to murder, usually a public figure.

clue.text: This will show Conservative in country at peak

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: India is a country
a tor is a rocky hill or peak, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A Tory MP shows up on a mountaintop in an Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator is a gauge or pointer that displays a reading.

clue.text: Dejected when diamonds had covered another card

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

indicators.note: covered says one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to have something is to own it, so had gives owned
a heart is a card of another suit

explanation.surface: A bridge player is glum when a diamond was trumped by a different card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' wraps the card inside the verb meaning had; the surface suggests trumping in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Downhearted describes someone low in spirits, depressed and disheartened.

clue.text: Duck resulting from good ball bowled around leg side

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps the other

parts.note: in cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach
in cricket the on side is the leg side

explanation.surface: A batsman's duck follows a decent wide delivery down the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a duck is also a score of nought, so the surface plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: The widgeon is a dabbling wild duck.

clue.text: Tongue-tied speaker has yet to start

indicators.note: to start says take the opening letter of each of the words around it

explanation.surface: A nervous orator has not yet begun the speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue-tied person is bashful and timid, unable to speak through nerves.

clue.text: One chimney in Scotland — it's put up to provide inducements.

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lum is the Scottish word for a chimney
the 's counts here as a letter

explanation.surface: A single Scottish chimney is built to encourage something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses ILUMITS to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that spur activity, incentives or inducements.

clue.text: Cannon without one letter is "canon"

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says one piece goes round another

parts.note: ordnance means artillery, guns such as cannon
the letter I looks like the figure one

explanation.surface: A pedant notes that cannon and canon differ by only one letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so ORDNANCE goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or decree, especially of the church, and an ordinance is an authoritative order.

clue.text: Girl joining political party in American city

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: NY is New York
ANC is the African National Congress, a South African party

explanation.surface: A young woman joins a party in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy is a common female first name, so the girl stands for it by example.

clue.text: Firm employing retired policeman bearing a title

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the whole piece is read from right to left
bearing means carrying, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: PC is a police constable
Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A company takes on an ex-officer who has been knighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' holds the knight's title inside the constable; 'retired' turns the whole run back.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and crisp both describe something with a hard, brittle texture, like fresh lettuce.

clue.text: Expression of contempt initially penned by playwright

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark written by a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an exclamation of impatience or disdain.

clue.text: Immortal unknown's left outside

indicators.note: left means gone away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: external means on the outside
X is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An immortal being of no known identity is shut out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unknown's left' means X has gone from EXTERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting, without end, as an immortal being is.

clue.text: Garland, the French one

parts.note: le is the French for the
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A garland is the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: Out of play, but still communicating

definitions.meaning: in rugby and football the touchlines bound the pitch; a ball beyond them is out of play

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby and football, touch is the area outside the sidelines.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch is the area beyond the sidelines, and being in contact is the everyday idiom.

clue.text: A small number in some trouble

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A handful of people are in some difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to bother or irritate them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Lay one's opinion to rest in formal discussion

parts.note: to lay a body to rest is to inter it
one's view is one's opinion

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside their views in the course of a formal talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay ... to rest' together means INTER; the phrase wraps round 'one's opinion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An interview is a formal meeting where questions are put and answered, for a job or for the press.
